newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close easier in consolidation.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close easier in consolidation.

text.p: French shares closed easier in consolidation from recent highs and on caution about a series of U.S. data including inflation, economic growth and unemployment, as well as the pending presidential elections, dealers said.
A higher start on Wall Street lifted shares from the day's lows in moderate volume during a French school holiday week.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 12.04 points or 0.56 percent at 2,150.39 while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,148.5 from 2,162.5 on Friday's close.
Volume was a modest 3.7 billion francs.
* "There is no fundamental uncertainty," a dealer said.
* Lagardere fell 6.93 percent to 154.50 on worries a poltical backlash to the planned sale of state-owned Thomson SA to Lagardere and South Korea's Daewoo Electronics.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Monday that the procedure followed by the government was beyond criticism. He said it was up to the independent privatisation commission to decide whether the sale could go ahead. The commission is expected to announce its verdict in early December.
* Rhone-Poulenc rose 2.04 percent to 150 francs in extended rise on Friday's nine-month results.
* L'Oreal closed 2.22 percent lower at 1,758 francs. Broker Natwest Sellier changed its recommendation on L'Oreal to "Hold" from "Accumulate" judging the share overvalued, fund managers said.

* Credit National shares up 7.29 percent at 259.10 francs with fund managers saying brokerage Cheuvreux de Virieu had switched its recommendation on the stock to "buy" from "sell". The share had recently been sliding amid speculation that the group could suffer a downgrading by ratings agencies.
* Canal Plus slips 0.32 percent to 1,247. The company announced an exclusive film rights deal with Universal.
* Shares in computer systems firms Sligos and Axime were suspended. The companies said they were in advanced alliance talks.
Axime is 26.1 percent held by Paribas Affaires Industrielles, a unit of Paribas, down 0.21 percent at 332.50 francs.

* Societe Generale slipped 0.36 percent to 554 francs despite saying it was considering selling off more of its share and property assets. It said a decision was not due before next year. The asset sales could trigger significant capital gains. -- Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
